use_when.text: Use a button to trigger a single, clear action : submit, confirm, save or start a flow.
Use Fill for the one primary action in a screen or section.
Use Outline or Transparent for secondary/tertiary actions alongside a primary Fill button.
Use the optional iconLeft/iconRight slots when an icon reinforces the label (e.g, a trailing chevron for "Next").
Use Icon Button instead of a labeled Button for single icon-only actions (favorite, close).

dont_use_when.text: Don't use a button to open an external link - >use a link/anchor style instead.
Don't enable both iconLeft and iconRight unless both icons add real meaning —> it crowds the label.
Don't use the error status as a generic "danger" style — > reserve it for a validation problem tied to the button's own action.
Don't ship a button without its focus variant — > it's required for keyboard accessibility, not optional polish.

values.default: Pins a cell of the matrix on so a story can show it standing still. `default` additionally lets the live :hover and :focus-visible states apply on their own.

a11y.fact: Renders a native `<button>` element, not a div with a click handler.
Sets the DOM `type` attribute from `htmlType`, which defaults to `button`, so the element does not submit a form unless a consumer passes `submit`.

Computes `disabled` as `disabled ?? status === 'disabled'`, so the disabled cell renders a genuinely disabled control rather than a grey-looking enabled one, and an explicit `disabled` prop still wins.

Spreads the consumer's remaining props onto the `<button>` before it sets `type`, `disabled` and the data attributes, so `aria-*` attributes passed in reach the element while `type` and `disabled` cannot be overridden by them.
Renders the `label` string as the button's only text content, in `.hds-button__label`, and sets no `aria-label`, so the accessible name is the `label` prop.
The `Info` glyph rendered into the icon slots carries `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable={false}`, so the icons are not in the accessibility tree and add nothing to the accessible name.
Draws the focus ring on `:focus-visible` with no `data-status` scoping, so the ring appears on keyboard focus at every status — including `error` and `hovered` — and not on a mouse click.
Sets `outline: none` on `:focus-visible` only for the element that already draws its own ring in the rule above, so focus is never left with no visible indicator.

gaps: variant_intent.type — the code states no purpose for `Fill`, `outline` or `transparent`; the doc comments at src/components/Button/Button.tsx#L30 and #L41 say only that it is the Figma `Type` property, so every value is null.
variant_intent.status — the code states a purpose only for `default` (src/components/Button/Button.tsx#L43-L47); `hovered`, `focus`, `disabled` and `error` are null.
variant_intent.htmlType — the doc comment at src/components/Button/Button.tsx#L55 states no purpose for `button`, `submit` or `reset`; every value is null.

placement — no story in src/components/Button/Button.stories.tsx places Button in a context. Every story renders it on the meta decorator's padded canvas (#L44-L50); `matrix (all 15)` (#L163) and `icon slots` (#L189) are bare grids of Buttons, not placements.

pairs_with — no story in src/components/Button/Button.stories.tsx renders another component beside Button; the only other component in the tree is the `Info` glyph composed inside it (src/components/Button/Button.tsx#L62).
